key_insight: Patch-wise PCA identifies a bandwidth bottleneck in pixel-space v-prediction: preserving noise-dominated minor components competes with modeling principal components.
engineering_relevance: Separating raw-state propagation from semantic modeling can make end-to-end pixel-space generation more trainable without a pretrained autoencoder.
method: Use patch-wise PCA, controlled experiments, and representation analysis to investigate prediction objectives.
Analyze x-prediction’s raw-input bypass and its implicit conditional-mean decoding under low-rank observations.
Introduce the Raw-injected Transformer (RiT), combining a lightweight raw-conditioned decoder with an output-side shortcut.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports restored effective v-prediction and competitive ImageNet 256×256 performance, but provides no numerical metrics.
watch_item: Generalization beyond the reported ImageNet setting remains unclear, and the conditional-mean decoder analysis assumes low-rank observations.
paper_title: What kills $v$-prediction? A Patch-wise PCA Perspective on Pixel-Space Flow Matching
